t: You're looking at the Royal London Hospital in Whitechapel, a large teaching hospital run by Barts Health NHS Trust. The current building has 1,248 beds and 34 wards, and opened in February 2012. It serves the City of London and Tower Hamlets, and provides specialist care for patients from across London. Several notable people died here. Emma Elizabeth Smith, the first of the Whitechapel murders, died here in 1888. So did the bacteriologist William Bulloch, and Amelia King, who was refused entry to the Women's Land Army in the Second World War because she was black, a decision that was debated in the House of Commons and later reversed.
